k01: Young King Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings at this high place of Gibeon.
That night, when the flames had died down, the king slept here, and the Lord appeared to him in a dream.
Think it over: what do you suppose the young king asked for that night?
k02: Two women stood before the king, each claiming one baby as her own son.
There were no witnesses — only two clashing voices echoing through the palace.
When King Solomon called for a sword, the true mother's heart was revealed.
k03: When the priests set the ark of the covenant in the Most Holy Place and came out, a cloud filled the temple.
The glory of the Lord filled the house, so the priests couldn't even stand to serve.
King Solomon knelt before the altar and spread out his hands toward heaven.
k04: Leading a caravan of camels loaded with spices, the queen of Sheba came from a far land in the south.
Solomon answered every hard question she had brought, without getting stuck on a single one.
When she saw the palace, the table and the servants, it took her breath away.
k05: On this hill stood high places for Chemosh of Moab and Molech of Ammon.
The one who built them was the very same King Solomon who had asked for wisdom at Gibeon.
As the king grew old, his foreign wives turned his heart toward other gods.
k06: I met young Jeroboam, whom Solomon had put in charge of the workers, on a road outside the city.
We were the only two out in the field. I tore the new cloak I was wearing into twelve pieces.
Listen closely — what do you think those pieces meant?
k07: When Solomon died, his son Rehoboam came here to Shechem to be made king.
The people asked him to lighten their heavy yoke, and the king told them to come back in three days.
The king rejected the elders' advice and answered harshly. The word I had spoken came true.
k08: Jeroboam, the first king of northern Israel, was gripped by one thought night after night.
He made two golden calves and set one here at Bethel and the other at Dan, in the far north.
He made priests of people who weren't Levites, and set festivals as he pleased.
k09: As Jeroboam was about to burn incense at this altar, a man of God from Judah cried out.
The hand the king stretched out, shouting Seize him!, shriveled up, and the altar split open and its ashes poured out.
But that man was fooled by the lie of an old prophet of Bethel, and went back and ate bread.
k10: I was old and my eyes were dim, but the Lord told me ahead of time who was coming.
Jeroboam's wife came to Shiloh in disguise to ask about her sick son.
When I heard footsteps at the door, I already knew who that woman was.
k11: In the fifth year of Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt came and carried off the treasures of the temple and the palace.
Even the gold shields Solomon had made were all loaded onto a foreign nation's carts.
So the guards stood holding bronze shields instead. Look at that dull yellow gleam.
k12: King Ahab married Jezebel, a princess of Sidon, and built a temple of Baal here in Samaria.
People believed Baal held the rain, and one by one they knelt at his altar.
That was when I stood before Ahab. It was heaven's turn to answer who truly gives the rain.
k13: After leaving the king, I came to this ravine as the word of the Lord told me.
When morning came, black wings flapped down and landed. In the evening too.
But the sky stayed shut, and the sound of the water grew thinner every day. Listen.
k14: In the land ruled by Jezebel's father, at this gate of Zarephath, I met a widow.
A handful of flour in a jar and a little oil in a jug were all that was left in her house.
When her son stopped breathing, I carried the boy up to the upper room and cried out.
k15: In the third year of the drought, all Israel and four hundred fifty prophets of Baal gathered on this mountain.
The prophets of Baal shouted from morning till evening, but there was no answer.
I rebuilt the Lord's broken altar with twelve stones and had water poured over the offering.
k16: Even after the fire fell, the sky stayed clear. I climbed to this summit and bowed down to the ground.
I sent my servant toward the sea, and at first there was nothing. He went back and forth seven times.
When the heavy rain poured down, I tucked up my robe and ran ahead of Ahab's chariot.
k17: When Jezebel heard what happened on Mount Carmel and sought my life, I got up and ran.
I left my servant at Beersheba, went alone into the wilderness and sank down in the shade of this broom tree.
As I slept, someone touched me. By my head lay bread baked on hot stones and a jar of water.
k18: I walked forty days and nights to reach this Mount Horeb, and spent the night in a cave.
A strong wind, an earthquake and a fire passed by, but the Lord was not in any of them.
After the fire came a low, gentle whisper. I covered my face with my cloak and stood.
k19: Back from Horeb, I came to Abel-meholah here, where twelve yoke of oxen were plowing.
As I passed Elisha, who was driving the last pair, I threw my cloak over him.
Elisha broke up his plow and yoke, made a fire, shared the meat, and followed me.
k20: King Ahab wanted Naboth's vineyard beside the palace, but Naboth wouldn't give it up.
Jezebel wrote letters in the king's name and set up false witnesses, and Naboth was stoned to death.
When Ahab came down to take that vineyard, I was standing there.
k21: On the threshing floor at this city gate, Ahab and Jehoshaphat king of Judah sat side by side.
Four hundred prophets shouted with one voice: Go up to Ramoth-gilead!
But Micaiah son of Imlah alone said something different. Listen to that one man.
k22: My master told me to stay here, but from Gilgal on I never left his side.
My master rolled up his cloak and struck the water of this Jordan, and the water parted.
A chariot of fire and horses of fire came between us, and my master went up in a whirlwind.
k23: This respected woman of Shunem built a small room on her roof so I could rest.
Her house had no son — and the next year, at that very season, a son was born.
When that child died, the woman hurried to Mount Carmel and took hold of my feet.
k24: Naaman, an Aramean general with leprosy, came to my door with his horses and chariots.
I didn't even go out — I sent a messenger. Naaman turned away in a rage.
His servants changed his mind, and Naaman came down into this Jordan and dipped himself in it.
k25: My disciples came to this riverside forest to cut beams for a place to live. I came with them.
As one of them was chopping a tree, the iron ax head flew off its handle and fell into the water.
I cut a stick and threw it at that spot. Watch the water closely.
k26: To capture me, the king of Aram sent a great army by night and surrounded this city of Dothan.
At dawn my servant went out, saw the army and cried out, not knowing what to do.
When he looked again, the hills all around us were full of horses and chariots of fire.
k27: The Aramean army surrounded this city until a donkey's head sold for eighty shekels of silver.
Four men with leprosy at the city gate went to the Aramean camp — and found it empty.
The Lord had made the Arameans hear the sound of a great army's chariots, and they ran.
k28: I sent one of my disciples with a flask of oil to Jehu at Ramoth-gilead.
Once anointed, Jehu drove his chariot like a madman and raced here to Jezreel.
Jehu's arrow pierced King Joram, and Jezebel, standing at her window, was thrown out of it.
k29: The day Athaliah killed all the royal family, Jehosheba stole away the baby Joash.
The child grew up hidden in this temple for six years.
In the seventh year, Jehoiada the priest put the crown on the boy and anointed him.
k30: When I was old and dying, Joash king of northern Israel came to me in tears.
I put my hands on the king's hands, opened the east window and had him shoot an arrow.
Then I told him to strike the ground with the arrows — and the king struck three times and stopped.
k31: Hoshea, the last king of northern Israel, stopped paying tribute to Assyria and was put in prison.
Even after its king was taken, this city held out three years before it finally fell.
The king of Assyria took the people captive and carried them off to Halah, the Habor River and the cities of the Medes.
k32: People were bowing down and burning incense before the bronze snake Moses had put on a pole.
Once it had been a sign that saved Israel, but now it had become a thing they bowed to instead of God.
Hezekiah, who became king at twenty-five, stood right in front of it.
k33: Rabshakeh, sent by Sennacherib king of Assyria, stood on the main road by the channel of the upper pool.
Eliakim, Shebna and Joah came out from the city, and on the wall the people held their breath.
Rabshakeh shouted even louder so all the people on the wall could hear. Still, the wall was silent.
k34: King Hezekiah put on sackcloth, went into the temple, and sent his officials to me.
Soon after, a letter came from the king of Assyria, and the king took it up to the temple.
He spread that letter out before the Lord, just as it was, and prayed.
k35: That night, the only thing the people in the city held on to was the word of the Lord I had brought.
When morning came, the Assyrian army that had seemed ready to swallow Judah never rose again.
Only a heavy silence settled over the camp. Look at this quiet morning.
k36: When King Hezekiah was sick and about to die, I went to him with the word of the Lord.
The king turned his face to the wall, prayed and wept bitterly.
Before I had even left the courtyard, I had to go back to him. Look at the shadow on the stairway of Ahaz.
k37: Merodach-baladan king of Babylon heard Hezekiah had been sick and sent envoys.
Hezekiah gladly opened everything to them — the silver and gold, the spices, even the armory.
Then I went to the king and asked where those men had come from.
k38: Long after Hezekiah's time, in the days of King Josiah, work to repair this temple was in full swing.
Shaphan the secretary read aloud before the king a book found in the temple.
As Josiah listened, he tore his clothes, and Hilkiah and Shaphan went to Huldah the prophetess.
k39: Josiah was the king who got rid of all the mediums, fortune-tellers and idols.
When Neco king of Egypt went up toward the Euphrates, Josiah came out here to Megiddo to block his way.
The king went into battle in disguise, was badly wounded by an arrow, and died in Jerusalem.
k40: The army of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon surrounded this city, and at last the food ran out.
The night the wall was broken through, King Zedekiah fled, but he was caught on the plains of Jericho.
Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, came and broke up the bronze pillars and the bronze Sea and carried them to Babylon.
k41: Jehoiachin king of Judah was locked away in prison far off here in Babylon.
He became king at eighteen and was carried off after three months. Thirty-seven years passed that way.
The song of those who wept by the rivers of Babylon, longing for Zion, still seems to echo here.
